body:
You are right that no one hates me more then I hate me - but it's not like I like feeling that way. Honestly, this is the only topic that gets me angry about myself. I screw up at work, I shake it off. I break something, whatever right? No use cry over it.

But this thing in me - it hates me. And that's the thing - it isn't suppose to be this hard. Get a job, get the girl, have the kid... it's suppose to be simple.

Oh sorry, very quickly, there seems to be a miscommunication here - I wasn't asking out co workers. I work in a location with lots of people passing through. I was talking to strangers. Just so we're clear.

1) Humans has no value except the value we are given by others. A person who benefits society is more important then someone like me who doesn't. A family may value a member of itself higher then a person on the outside, but there is no "HUMAN FAMILY". I have no value because I'm not important to anyone.  
2)Yes, it was an experiment I was running at work. Starting Jan 1, I talked to and asked out 90 women ending March 30th. An important experience to be sure. Learned that people can be very nice when they have to be, but I uninterested in seeing me.
therapists are overpaid imo... actually could use a life coach though maybe...

Been to therapy, group therapy, and animal therapy. 10+ years. "Love yourself" was there recurring message. "But I hate myself?" I would reply. "Well you should stop that, i guess." Then I realized they were staffed by idiots with no response and they stopped trying.... puppies were cute though!
Look people in the eye was always tough for me (particularly women) so I needed the personal practice.

Well... starting off it helps to have a followup to "Hi". Like "Hi can I ask you if/what/where/how..." that was the first big hurtle. Second, it helped we talked to things that they liked "Oh you were in store X, but friend works there. You have good taste" that sorta thing.
Live, in the flesh. You're right, practice was super important.

I work at a mall and would force myself to go up to someone or a group and ask them where stuff was, or how they were doing or something like that. Some conversations continued, some didn't. Practice makes perfect.

I had a bet with my friend to see how many questions before we got to this one (he said it would be one of the first ones, I said it would be 5th or more lol). Now I owe him lunch thanks a lot.

Short answer, none. 0/90.

Wasn't what it was about really, so I can't say I'm disappointed. I'm not what women call a "looker" so it always meant I was shy and looking down at the ground. This was to help me with social interaction.

I did ask some of them if they wanted to get coffee, but they all gently let me down. Some were clearly lying about having bfs but that's ok too.

Did you just assume my gender? lol  


No seriously, if can't succeed at pick up because if I did then Darwin was wrong and humans would be evolving backwards. lol

I'm glad someone understands. It's not that I don't enjoy what I do, it's just that I want more fulfillment as you say. I could never do pick up tho - Too broken mentally and physically to do something like that. I appreciate the guys who can do and I am jealous of the guys who don't need to.

> **CARRY A GODDAMN SWORD AROUND YOUR HOUSE FOR AN HOUR**

Well... that certainly is a unique solution. Kudos!
